title: Reserved GPU Pools SLA: Quantified Throughput SLOs, Error-Budgeting, and Contract Remedies
creator: Elena Morales
description: Goal: Produce a complete, legally-reviewed SLA and supporting runbook for Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) that quantifies throughput guarantees, defines an error budget model, prescribes remediation and credit calculations, and clarifies interactions with autoscaling and fleet controls. Deliverables: 1) Contract-ready SLA language (two variants: enterprise and mid-market), 2) Error budget math and billing credit formula, 3) Measurement queries and dashboard widgets in Console, 4) Runbook for breach detection and customer notifications, 5) Legal sign-off and playbook for renewals/penalties.
acceptance_criteria: Draft SLA text for enterprise and mid-market reviewed and accepted by Legal (document link in links).
Error budget defined per calendar month with explicit calculation and example scenarios (20% buffer examples).
Telemetry queries (PromQL/SQL) validated against historical data and added to Console as an SLO dashboard widget.
Automated monthly SLO report produced showing percent of time met, error budget consumed, and any applied credits.
Runbook documented with roles, escalation path, and cron jobs for periodic verification; engineering and SRE sign-off obtained.
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Decided SLO baseline will be defined against 'promised throughput' (customer-configured reserved tokens/sec equivalent) rather than aggregate cluster capacity to avoid noisy neighbors affecting SLAs.
2026-03-08: Agreed error budget window = calendar month; unused error budget does NOT roll over. Rationale: aligns with billing cycles and legal simplicity.

2026-03-09: Chosen remediation tiers: (a) monitoring + customer alert; (b) service credit formula; (c) accelerated support/engineering triage for repeated breaches. Legal wants explicit cap on yearly credits.

2026-03-11: Autoscaling interaction: SLA applies only to 'allocated' capacity (the reserved pool). If autoscaling is enabled, we guarantee effective throughput = reserved capacity + configured burst capacity up to X% (see attached calculations). Warm-up periods (scale-out latency) are excluded within a 5-minute window after autoscale events. Engineering requested a 20% burst headroom assumption for contract math; legal requested clarifying language to avoid ambiguous promises.
sample_sla_clauses: Service Commitment: Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that Customer's reserved GPU pool delivers the Promised Throughput at a monthly availability of 99.5% measured at the pool level unless otherwise stated in the Order Form.

Definitions: 'Promised Throughput' = Customer's configured reserved capacity expressed as requests-per-second equivalent (RPS-e) and documented in the Order Form. 'Availability' = proportion of the monthly measurement window where measured throughput >= 95% of Promised Throughput, excluding agreed maintenance windows.

Error Budget: For each calendar month, Error Budget = (1 - SLO) * Measurement Window. Breaches consume error budget in proportion to time and severity. If Error Budget is exhausted, Redwood will (a) allocate engineering resources for mitigation, and (b) apply Service Credits as specified below.

Service Credits: If a monthly breach occurs such that Availability < SLO, Customer shall be eligible for a service credit equal to min(25% of monthly Dedicated fee, Calculated Credit), where Calculated Credit = (SLO - Availability) / SLO * Monthly Dedicated fee. Credits are the sole remedy and will not exceed the capped amount. Credits are applied after validation and may require a claim within 30 days of the monthly report.

Autoscaling & Burst: When autoscaling is enabled, Promised Throughput for SLA calculation will include the configured baseline reserved capacity plus explicit burst allowance specified on the Order Form. Scale-out latency (the first 5 minutes following an autoscale trigger) is excluded from SLA measurements.
measurement_spec: Metric sources: runtime throughput counters (per-pool), token/tokenized request counts from ingress, and request-latency histograms. Primary signal = 1-minute aggregated RPS-e reported by pool agent.
Windowing: Evaluate Availability per calendar month; group by minute and compute percent of minutes meeting >=95% Promised Throughput threshold.
Data retention & audit: Store raw minute-level telemetry for 13 months to allow audit and disputed claims. Audit logs used for credit validation shall be exportable to customer upon approved request.

Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance (72h prior notification) and customer-caused outages (e.g., misconfigured networking) are excluded from measurements per contract. Force majeure and third-party cloud provider outages will be handled per standard force majeure clause.
runbook_highlights: Automated detection job runs hourly; if error budget consumption exceeds 10% in first 7 days, auto-create incident and notify PM and SRE Slack channel #dedicated-sla.
Monthly SLO job produces report and posts to customer-facing portal; customers must file claims within 30 days if they dispute credit calculations.
On confirmed breach: apply credit per formula, create postmortem if breach severity > P1, schedule follow-up with account team within 5 business days.
